clue.text: Where to get old bangers for females to rent in Wales

parts.note: a car mart is a used-car market, where old bangers (decrepit cars) are sold
hens are female birds, so females can be hens
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: Someone looking for cheap old cars, or for women to hire, somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage and also for a battered old car; here it is the car. The definition is loose: a Welsh county, placed 'in Wales'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmarthenshire is a county of south-west Wales, so the clue places it by its country.

clue.text: Plot with a commission to destroy the global view

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks them up so their letters can be built into something new

explanation.surface: A plot, backed by a commission, to wreck internationalist thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to destroy' rearranges PLOT, A and COMMISSION, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmopolitanism is the outlook that sees all humanity as one world community, a global view.

clue.text: Change sides with 10 as quotient

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's party for the other side
the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Switching sides and taking ten as the result of a division.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it is read as the letters its two figures resemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotient, the result of dividing one quantity by another, is a ratio.

clue.text: Don't do it to the first two on the mark

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes before it

parts.note: the first two letters of the alphabet are A and B
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Advice to refrain, aimed at the two front-runners on the starting line.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from doing something, which is what 'Don't do it' tells you.

clue.text: Lesbian clan concealing publicity

indicators.note: a word concealing another holds it inside itself

parts.note: a clan is a tribe
an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A group of women keeping their existence out of the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribade is an old word for a lesbian, from the Greek for 'rub'.

clue.text: Everlastin?

parts.note: a word meaning everlasting printed without its final letter, as if it had lost its end

explanation.surface: A misprinted word with its last letter gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is EVERLASTING without its end: a synonym of the answer, cut 'end less'. The question mark marks the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting never stops, which is to be without an end.

clue.text: What brings warm air to the French is a fast one

parts.note: a south wind, S WIND, brings warm air from the south
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A southerly breeze reaching the French is a quick thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fast one' is from the idiom 'pull a fast one', to cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast one is a trick or deception, a con played on someone, as in 'pull a fast one'.

clue.text: Leaving nothing out isn't yet without brief account

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
letters that are out are disordered, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: A/C is the short form of account

explanation.surface: A will that leaves nothing out, not yet written up as a short report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ISNT YET into INTESTY, and 'without' puts it around AC. The surface makes 'Leaving nothing out' one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestacy is dying without a will, so leaving no testament and no bequests.

clue.text: Sun of York who further dated revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns everything over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A king whose dates were pushed back by a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges WHO FURTHER DATED. Shakespeare's Richard III opens with 'this sun of York', meaning Edward IV, whose badge was the sun in splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward IV is the 'sun of York' of Richard III's opening speech, a pun on son and his sun badge.

clue.text: Much of day is left, leaving remaining horses happy

parts.note: Sat is the shortened form of Saturday, most of the day's name

indicators.note: the letter for left leaving a word means it is taken out

parts.note: the field is the horses still running in a race

explanation.surface: Most of the day remains, and the last runners are content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes L out of FIELD to make FIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be satisfied is to be content and pleased, much the same as happy.

clue.text: Maybe I won't be dragged along

indicators.note: maybe suggests another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that they refuse to be pulled along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges the letters of I WONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in tow is being pulled behind another vehicle or person.

clue.text: Dragonflies get round fellow with a word of appreciation

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a don is a fellow of a college
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Insects encircling a college fellow and saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Odonata is the scientific order of insects comprising dragonflies and damselflies.

clue.text: Ensured result for last to get product

indicators.note: the result of working the letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A guaranteed outcome for whoever is last in line for the goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' rearranges ENSURED.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the final consumer, the last person in the chain to receive a product.

parts.note: 26 across is INFERNO, and Dis is the classical underworld and Dante's city of hell
6 down is SWINDLE, and a con is a swindle
the number ten, read literally here
8 down is EDWARD THE FOURTH, and Ted is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A list of cross-references said to be unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Each number stands for a synonym of that entry, except 10, which is simply the number. 'not 9' is 'not SATISFIED'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discontented means being dissatisfied, the opposite of the 9 across answer.

clue.text: Receiver's crime

definitions.meaning: read as 'of receiver', where a fence is slang for a receiver of stolen goods
a breach of the law, a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A handler of stolen goods committing a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: the possessive 's is read as 'of', and a fence is a dealer in stolen goods, so 'Receiver's' gives OF FENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a crime.

clue.text: Unrestrained comment of jury on parasitic person

parts.note: free means unrestrained
a rider is a comment or recommendation a jury adds to its verdict

explanation.surface: An outspoken remark from a jury about a sponger.
explanation.definitionFit: A free rider benefits from others' efforts without paying, like a parasite.

clue.text: See 13
Royal family's skill with slow cooker?

parts.note: a stew is cooked slowly, so it stands for slow cooking
art is skill

explanation.surface: A dynasty known for its talent with a casserole pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Stewart is a spelling of Stuart, the Scottish and later British royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stewarts were the royal house of Scotland, later as Stuarts of England too.

clue.text: See 13
Arranging flowers like bananas? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the phrase: the run sits inside it, with letters left off each end

explanation.surface: A flower display likened to a bunch of bananas, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' marks a run inside LIKE BANANAS with the L and the NAS left off; the question mark admits the comparison is silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arrangement.

clue.text: A creature having tail removed first made madder

indicators.note: a creature with its tail removed loses its last letter

parts.note: a lizard is a creature
I is the Roman numeral one, as in Elizabeth I, the first

explanation.surface: An animal that lost its tail first went crazier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madder' looks like 'crazier', but it is the dye plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Alizari is a name for madder, the plant and the red dye made from its root.

clue.text: A model fed up with wearing clothes

parts.note: the Model T was the classic Ford car
tired means fed up

explanation.surface: A fashion model sick of having to keep dressing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attired is dressed, wearing clothes.

clue.text: At the present time see return with a flourish

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month, the present time

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Right now, look back and sweep on with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses ELY to YLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in style means doing it with panache, with a flourish.

clue.text: One lot of stones at home of dictator

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all of it: the end is dropped

parts.note: diamonds are precious stones
in means at home

explanation.surface: A heap of stones at a tyrant's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot of' keeps DIAM from DIAMONDS. Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Idi Amin ruled Uganda as a military dictator from 1971 to 1979.

clue.text: Fairly relaxed like this drinker — about time

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it

parts.note: a fish, as in 'drinks like a fish', stands for a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drinker who is somewhat at ease, getting on in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside FISH to make FTISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Softish means somewhat soft, so fairly easy-going or relaxed.

clue.text: See 13
Relief supplied by thermals?

parts.note: thermals are rising warm air currents that lift things, but relief here is aid flown in

explanation.surface: Comfort given by warm underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Thermals look like warm underclothes; they are rising currents of warm air, and the relief is emergency aid delivered by aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift is delivery of supplies or relief by aircraft.

clue.text: Get number from fire

parts.note: to get someone's meaning is to infer it

explanation.surface: Receiving a figure from a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, raging fire.

clue.text: This will locate drama school correctly

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school
correctly means right, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A guide that helps you find a theatre academy properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a system that detects and locates distant objects by reflected radio waves.

clue.text: Source of paper, ink and rubber

definitions.text: Source of paper, ink and rubber

parts.words: Source of paper, ink and rubber
parts.note: a country that gives its name to a thin paper, a black ink and an eraser

explanation.surface: Where the stationery cupboard's supplies come from.
explanation.walkthrough: India paper, India ink and India rubber are all named for the country.
explanation.definitionFit: India gives its name to India paper, India ink and India rubber.

clue.text: Rest of article put in souvenir

indicators.note: one piece put in another sits inside it

parts.note: a souvenir is a reminder of a place
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The rest of an item placed in a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Ride off a little way to old city in time to get led up the aisle

parts.note: March is a time of year, a month

indicators.note: the word is off, gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an inch is a small distance
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be setting off on a short ride to an ancient city before being walked down the aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges RIDE; 'in' sends the pieces into the month. 'led up the aisle' is the idiom for being taken to the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Being led up the aisle is the idiom for being married in church.
